newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dana Petroleum makes bid for Petroceltic.
newsitem.headline: Dana Petroleum makes bid for Petroceltic.

text.p: Exploration group Dana Petroleum said on Friday that it was offering nine shares for every four Petroceltic shares, giving a value of 3.05 million punts to the entire share capital of Petroceltic.
The offer gives a value of 34.875 Irish pence for each Petroceltic share, Dana said in a statement.
"I believe this offer represents an opportunity for Dana to secure a stream of high quality royalty revenue to augment our Russian earnings," Dana chairman Charles Smith said.
Petroceltic's main asset is a royalty interest in the Kinsale Head and Ballycotton gas fields, situated off the south coast of Ireland, which are operated by Marathon.
Petroceltic also has offshore exploration interests in Ireland, western Australia and west Africa.

Smith said the broadening of Dana's portfolio carries the full support of its Russian partners "who may co-venture with Dana in certain of the new areas where their expertise and experience will add value".

Dana's current operations are all based in western Siberia where it owns 50 percent of YoganOil, an operator of the south Vat-Yoganskoye oil field. It has 30 percent of YuganskOil, an operator of Sortymskoye oil field and five percent of Evikhon, a Russian oil and gas company.
